standard.title: Agro Textiles — HDPE Laminated Woven Lay Flat Tube and Its Fittings for Use in Rain Irrigation System — Specification
standard.sector: Technical Textiles / Technical Textiles for Agro-tech

sectional_committee.name: Technical Textiles for Agro-Tech Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies requirements, dimensions, testing methods, and field installation guidelines for UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene (HDPE) laminated woven lay flat tubes (commonly referred to as rain pipes or perforated lay flat tubes) and their fittings used in rain irrigation systems.
standard.scope: This standard specifies requirements, dimensions, testing methods, and field installation guidelines for UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene (HDPE) laminated woven lay flat tubes (commonly referred to as rain pipes or perforated lay flat tubes) and their fittings used in rain irrigation systems.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Agro Textiles (Quality Control) Order' (Agrotech QCO) issued by the Ministry of Textiles, Government of India, all HDPE laminated woven lay flat tubes and fittings supplied for rain irrigation systems must conform to IS 17728:2021 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified rain pipes in India is a statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to synthetic irrigation piping systems.
requirements: Each dispatched bundle or roll of lay flat tube must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and standard designation (IS 17728).

Tapes used in weaving the fabric must be manufactured from UV-stabilized high-density polyethylene granules. If carbon black is added, it must contain a minimum of 2.5 percent of carbon black by mass with satisfactory dispersion tested per IS 2530. The tape width must be at least 2.0 mm, and linear density must be at least 77.7 Tex (700 Denier).

The manufacturer must declare the range of working pressure between the minimum working pressure (Pmin) and maximum working pressure (Pmax) within which the perforated lay flat tube operates effectively.
The woven lay flat tube fabric must demonstrate high breaking strength. Average breaking strength in N must be determined under standard crosshead traverse speeds of 300 ± 15 mm/min.

The fabric must resist physical puncture. Average puncture resistance must be calculated from 5 tested specimens clamped in a circular ring clamp (grooved with an O-ring or sandpaper) using a solid steel rod plunge attached to a load indicator.
The lay flat tube specimen must pass bending tests without physical cracking. It passes if none of the first 10 bends fails, or not more than 2 fail in a total sample of 20 bends.

To prevent orifice tearing or warping under severe summer sun, hot water is circulated through a 1-meter sample at maximum working pressure (Pmax). The percentage change in hole diameter must be less than 5 percent.

Water flow rate is measured in litres per hour per metre (l/h/m) across the declared working pressure range (Pmin, Pnom, Pmax). Flow rates for nominal diameters—including standard sizes 32 mm and 40 mm—must stay within ±5 percent of the manufacturer's declared value.

Under nominal working pressure, a 40 m length (for 32 mm size) or 45 m length (for 40 mm size) lay flat tube is tested on flat ground. The farthest spray throw distance must meet specified agricultural irrigation bounds.

A standard commercial rain pipe kit consists of: a) Main/Sub-main line (IS 16627); b) Perforated lay flat tube; c) Pump-to-main line connectors; d) Sub-main-to-lay flat tube connectors; e) Tube-to-tube jointers.
Prior to storage, the entire system must be dried completely. The lay flat tube must be stored securely to prevent structural damage from rodents.

The sub-main line is branched using metal or plastic TEEs based on internal diameter (e.g. 75mm x 63mm for a 75mm main). Hoses are secured on connectors up to the rubber flat ring and tightened with clamps to guarantee no leakage.
For assembly, the lock ring must be pulled forward, the rain pipe put on the start connector, and the ring pulled backward towards the rain pipe properly to ensure no leakage.
